newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says copper capped by producers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says copper capped by producers.

text.p: Australia base metals miner MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that world copper prices were being supported by strong short term fundamentals but were being capped by producer selling.
"Since last June ... base metals prices have about managed to hold the depressed levels to which they had fallen," chairman Bruce Vaughan told the annual meeting.
"Copper prices are supported by strong short term fundamentals," Vaughan said.

"It is reported that LME copper stocks are currently at an all-time low," he said. "However, prices remain capped by producer selling based on the expectation of supply increases over the next couple of years."
"The real market price for copper is further exacerbated by the continuing uncertainties caused by the international copper trading fiasco earlier this year," Vaughan said.
Vaughan said zinc prices continued to be disappointing, moving sideways since June, while lead prices had retreated from the strong levels seen mid-year.
"This said, it is noteworthy that a number of industry observers are forecasting significant increases in zinc prices and worthwhile increases in lead prices within the next year or two," he said.
Vaughan said precious metals prices were also struggling.
MIM shares were four cents higher at A$1.64 at 11.40 a.m. (0040 GMT).
